title: Does validate leak whether a login exists
sends: Policy mode: a login that cannot exist (`nobody-<random>@example.com`) placed in turn in `groups`, `tagOwners`, an `acls` `src`, an `ssh` `src`, a test `src`, and as an object key
expected: Every position yields either the same rejection or a pass that does not depend on the user existing
branch: If a position distinguishes existing from absent users, the subject rule already covers it (keys and values); the guide names the positions

observations.label: a login that cannot exist, in groups
observations.expect: the same rejection, or a pass that does not depend on the user existing

observations.label: a login that cannot exist, in tagOwners
observations.expect: the same rejection, or a pass that does not depend on the user existing

observations.label: a login that cannot exist, as an acls src
observations.expect: the same rejection, or a pass that does not depend on the user existing

observations.label: a login that cannot exist, as an ssh src
observations.expect: the same rejection, or a pass that does not depend on the user existing

observations.label: a login that cannot exist, as a test src
observations.expect: the same rejection, or a pass that does not depend on the user existing

observations.label: a login that cannot exist, as an object key (in hosts)
observations.expect: the same rejection, or a pass that does not depend on the user existing

checks.name: an accepted position exists and none carries a warning about the login
acceptance does not vary across the six positions
every rejection is the same rejection
